title: How Human Cannonballs Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how human cannonball acts work, covering the history from the Farini projector and Lulu (1870s) through Zazzle (Rosa Richter, 1880) and the Zacchini family, the physics of compressed-air launch and g-forces, safety and net landings, test dummies, the Elvin Bale Hong Kong accident, Matt Cranch's fatal 2011 act, a DARPA human-launch patent idea, and a fatal-accident tally. The episode opens with banter about Kaboom cereal and Hunter S. Thompson's cannon-shot remains, and closes with a listener mail about a haunted Adirondack home with an Underground Railroad tunnel and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and Hunter S. Thompson
segments.summary: Hosts joke about Kaboom cereal and a clown-themed cannon, then discuss Hunter S. Thompson's cremated remains being fired from a cannon and whether Josh wants his own body shot from a cannon.

segments.title: Myth of gunpowder and early history
segments.summary: The hosts explain that human cannonballs are not launched with gunpowder but with a piston and fake boom and flash. They trace the history to the Farini projector (1871), Lulu's 30-foot flight caught on a trapeze, and Zazzle's 1880 cannon flight that injured her back.

segments.title: Physics and forces of launch
segments.summary: The hosts describe the compressed-air piston launch at roughly 3,000 to 6,000 psi, the capsule inside the barrel, launch speeds up to about 70 mph and distances up to 200 feet, and the nine g launch and twelve g impact forces, compared with the Dodonpa coaster.

segments.title: Planning, test dummies and net landings
segments.summary: Operators account for wind, body weight, humidity and obstacles. Test dummies are fired first to dial in trajectory, and the net is best hit in its rear third to avoid bouncing backward.

segments.title: Circus families, deaths and accidents
segments.summary: The Zacchini family performed from the 1920s into the 1990s, with Mario shot over two Ferris wheels. John Weiss fired about 5,000 times. Thirty of roughly fifty human cannonballs have died, per historian A. H. Cox. David Smith Jr. and his family are described, and the DARPA patent idea for shooting responders onto buildings is discussed.

segments.title: Elvin Bale accident and Matt Cranch death
segments.summary: Elvin Bale overshot his air bag in Hong Kong after a wet test dummy gave misleading results, leaving him paralyzed. Matt Cranch died in April after his net collapsed. The Zacchini sister and brother collided mid-air in a double-barrel stunt and she broke her back.

segments.title: Closing pointer and promo
segments.summary: Hosts point listeners to the HowStuffWorks search bar for more on human cannonballs and promote a video podcast, with a sponsor line.

segments.title: Underground Railroad tunnel listener mail
segments.summary: A listener describes a haunted Adirondack home in Johnsburg, New York, with a hidden Underground Railroad tunnel beneath a barn that exits into a strawberry patch.
